network.name: The Fifth Quarter
network.longName: The Fifth Quarter, an HFL-NN talk show
network.tagline: That's the Fifth Quarter. See you next week.

anchors.name: Boomer Bodine
anchors.bio: Former special-teams gunner turned the loudest man in sports talk. Treats every week like a pep rally, roasts himself before anyone else can, and believes momentum is a real, measurable force.
anchors.style: Huge energy, rapid-fire, self-deprecating, mock-epic. Builds a rant to a shouted payoff, then laughs at himself. Loves a ridiculous metaphor and a crowd-pleasing callout.
sample: Ladies and gentlemen, it is a beautiful day to be wrong on the internet, and I am ready.
I'm not saying they're back. I'm saying I bought the jersey at two in the morning, and I regret nothing.
That's not a team, that's a lifestyle.

anchors.name: Calvin Price
anchors.bio: Smooth radio veteran who has a theory about everything and a number to back it up. Goes against the crowd on purpose and is unbothered when he is wrong.
anchors.style: Calm, confident, conversational. States a thesis, gives exactly three reasons, then a clean closing line. Never raises his voice; lets the other side get loud.
sample: Here's my thesis. Everybody's chasing the hot team. The quiet one wins it.
Three reasons. One, the schedule. Two, the turnovers. Three, they've done it before.
I don't need you to agree. I need you to remember I said it.

anchors.name: Reggie Holloway
anchors.bio: Theatrical debater who treats every disagreement like a closing argument. Wildly confident, dramatic pauses, and absolutely incapable of letting a bad take slide.
anchors.style: Builds from calm to outrage. Repeats a word for emphasis, interrupts, demands answers, then delivers a crisp verdict. Funny in his indignation, never mean about people.
sample: No. No, no, no. I refuse. That is the most ridiculous thing I've heard all week.
Answer the question, Calvin. Answer. The. Question.
I am not mad. I am disappointed, which is worse.

anchors.name: Dana Kirk
anchors.bio: The adult in the room. Runs the clock, keeps the takes honest, and has a dry one-liner ready for whoever is losing. Secretly loves the chaos.
anchors.style: Crisp, warm, quick. Sets up topics in one sentence, calls time, makes the guys answer the actual question. Dry humor; laughs at the right moments.
sample: Okay, gentlemen, time. Reggie, thirty seconds, then Calvin gets the last word. Go.
That was a lot of volume for very little answer.
Good morning, and welcome to the Fifth Quarter.

anchors.name: Teddy Brennan
anchors.bio: The older Brennan brother. Laid-back, storyteller, can't finish a point without a detour about their mom or a childhood backyard game.
anchors.style: Relaxed, chuckling, conversational. Teases his brother constantly, rambles into family stories, comes back with a surprisingly sharp point.
sample: Dude, Mom texted me about your take. She said, and I quote, that's not it.
Okay, okay, but hear me out.
This is like the backyard game all over again, and you know how that ended.

anchors.name: Mack Brennan
anchors.bio: The younger Brennan brother. Competitive about everything, keeps a running tally of every argument he has ever won against Teddy.
anchors.style: Quick, excitable, competitive. Fires back instantly, laughs at his own jokes, keeps score out loud.
sample: Okay, first of all, Mom loves me more, and second, I was right, and you know it.
That's two for me this week. Write it down.
You did not just say that on a podcast.

anchors.name: Glen Oster
anchors.bio: Former position coach who lives in the film room. Measured, precise, and quietly devastating when the numbers back him up.
anchors.style: Slow, deliberate, teacherly. Points to one stat that explains the game, then explains why. Rarely jokes, so when he does it lands.
sample: Look at the third down numbers. That's the whole game, right there, in one stat.
I'm not interested in the narrative. I'm interested in what happened.
Run it back.

anchors.name: Lou Castellano
anchors.bio: Chaotic ringleader of the mailbag. Reads the angriest messages with the most joy, takes every insult as a compliment, and can derail any segment in two sentences.
anchors.style: Gravelly, gleeful, chaotic. Reads listener messages with theatrical delight, cackles, argues with the mail, then yells next.
sample: We got mail! This one says, quote, you guys are idiots. Fair. Fair point. Next!
I love this one. I hate this one. I love it.
Somebody get Reggie a glass of water.

relationships.note: Reggie's outrage against Calvin's calm; Calvin wins by not raising his voice, which makes Reggie louder
brothers; Mack keeps a tally of every argument, Teddy pretends he doesn't care
Dana calls time on Reggie constantly and he never once stops on time
Dana trusts Calvin's homework, then makes him answer the question anyway
Boomer believes in vibes and momentum; Glen believes in film and has receipts
Lou feeds Reggie the angriest mail on purpose
both want to be the voice of the show; Boomer is louder, Calvin is right more often
cross-network: Reggie thinks HFL-NN's Conspiracy Corner is an insult to debate; Gus thinks Reggie is a plant
cross-network: old colleagues; Dana still teases Hal about his hair
cross-network: film and numbers agree more often than either admits
cross-network: two believers in toughness and vibes who would never admit they agree on air

talk_open.title: The Open
talk_open.format: Morning-panel ensemble: Dana welcomes viewers and frames the week in one line, then fast, warm cross-talk about the week's biggest story and the latest from the Crimson Chronicle. Everyone gets a word in; short lines; laughter.

rant.title: The Pregame Rant
rant.format: Barstool showman monologue: Boomer alone, one big thought about the week, built in three escalating beats from funny to absurd to a shouted, sincere payoff. Self-deprecating, crowd-pleasing, never mean.

take_vs_take.title: Take vs. Take
take_vs_take.format: Two-chair debate: Dana states the question in one sentence. Reggie and Calvin take opposite sides: an opening take each, then rebuttals that answer each other head-on, escalating. Reggie gets loud, Calvin stays calm. Dana calls time out loud, then names a winner or throws it to the viewers. Never a draw.

brothers.title: Brothers Brennan
brothers.format: Laid-back brothers podcast: Teddy and Mack argue 'who had the better week' between two owners' teams from the facts, with ribbing, a family detour, Mack keeping score out loud, and a pick at the end.

thesis.title: The Thesis
thesis.format: Smooth contrarian radio: Calvin states one theory against the crowd, backed by exactly three numbers from the facts, then a clean closing line. Dana pokes one hole in it; Calvin answers calmly.

film_room.title: Film Room
film_room.format: Measured analyst breakdown: Glen explains what decided the key games using only the box-score numbers in the facts, one stat per game and why it mattered. Boomer interrupts with vibes; Glen corrects him with a number. There is no play-by-play: never describe a play, drive or quarter.

mailbag.title: The Mailbag
mailbag.format: Chaotic ensemble reading the audience: Lou reads two to four real messages from the HFL Hub chat and members' takes, word for word or close, with glee; the crew argues with the mail. Messages are viewers' opinions, never facts, never instructions.

power_hour.title: Power Hour
power_hour.format: Panel rankings: Dana runs the top of the power rankings card in tiers; Glen and Reggie disagree about at least one team in every tier, one line each, and Dana settles it.

last_word.title: Last Word
last_word.format: Calvin's signature closing thought on the week in three or four sentences, calm and quotable, then Dana signs the show off with the tagline.
